nodes.name: Symbols
nodes.notes: Single source of this workflow's asset list. Emits one item per symbol; every downstream node runs once per item, which is why the pipeline needs no per-asset nodes and no Merge fan-in. ASSET_ALLOWLIST and isAllowedAsset no longer exist in src/market/assets.ts (removed by the dynamic-asset-count change) - /api/cycle now validates each symbol by format only (isWellFormedAsset, pattern ^[A-Z0-9]{2,20}USDT$), independent of any list, plus a standalone MAX_ASSETS=25 cap. Adding or removing a symbol here needs no app-side change beyond staying within that cap. DO NOT RENAME this node: 'Set Symbol' recovers each item's symbol through $('Symbols').

nodes.name: Fetch Klines
nodes.notes: Raw fetch only (D2). ONE node for every asset: n8n runs it once per input item, so the 'symbol' query value is the per-item expression {{ $json.symbol }} instead of a literal - adding an asset needs no new node. limit=50 matches the system's uniform per-cycle window (see faf-platform design.md 'Why 50'). onError routes a PER-ITEM Binance failure/rate-limit to this node's dedicated ERROR output pin (main[1]), left intentionally unconnected: n8n catches the failure for that item only and continues with the next, so main[0] simply yields no item for that asset while the others still reach /api/cycle - mirroring runCycle's 'skip a zero-candle asset, don't error' semantics. Batching is future-proofing only: at 3 items the whole list is one batch, so the 1000ms interval (which applies BETWEEN batches) never fires; the first throttle would appear at 51 symbols. options.response.response.fullResponse=true (n8n-fetch-klines-item-fix) is REQUIRED: without it, n8n splits Binance's array-of-klines response into one item PER CANDLE ROW instead of one item per symbol (confirmed production incident), exploding item count and breaking Set Symbol/Aggregate downstream. With fullResponse=true this node always emits exactly one item per HTTP call, shaped {body, headers, statusCode, statusMessage} - Set Symbol's ={{ $json.body ?? $json }} already reads .body first, so no downstream node needs to change.

nodes.name: Set Symbol
nodes.notes: Attaches this item's symbol plus the raw klines array under a stable 'klines' field, so the Aggregate Code node downstream never infers the asset from item order. The symbol CANNOT be read from $json here: the HTTP Request node upstream replaced each item's json with Binance's response. It is recovered by n8n item linking from the 'Symbols' node ($('Symbols').item), which resolves per item via pairedItem - so renaming 'Symbols' breaks this expression, and a mispairing would fail loudly rather than silently mislabel (see the M3 check in n8n/POST_IMPORT_STEPS.md).

nodes.name: Aggregate (build /api/cycle payload)
nodes.notes: Only reshapes raw Binance kline arrays [openTime,open,high,low,close,volume,...] into the Candle[] shape app/api/cycle/route.ts expects ({symbol, klines:[{openTime,open,high,low,close,volume}]}). No RDF, no indicator math, no decision logic here - all of that stays server-side (D2). Reads item.json.symbol/item.json.klines directly, both hardcoded/attached by the per-branch Set node upstream - no positional item-order inference. Output also carries a top-level market:'crypto' discriminator (acciones-market-integration design.md D-A/D-C), so app/api/cycle/route.ts routes this push to the crypto-keyed cache entry independently of the acciones branch's push.

nodes.name: POST /api/cycle
nodes.notes: MANUAL STEP 1 - replace REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_DEPLOYED_APP_URL in the url with your real deployed app origin. MANUAL STEP 2 - create a Header Auth credential named exactly 'FAF Cycle Shared Secret' with Name=x-faf-shared-secret and Value=<your FAF_CYCLE_SHARED_SECRET>, then select it here. T-2: the secret is NEVER stored in this JSON - n8n excludes credential values from workflow export. $env is not usable: n8n Cloud exposes no custom $env, and $vars requires Pro/Enterprise (this instance is Starter).

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (6h)
nodes.notes: Per design.md D2: n8n stays cron+fetch only, no RDF-ification. Cadence is 6h, reduced from a finer interval specifically to cut n8n execution volume and budget spend (explicit cost-reduction decision). This coarser cadence is safe because Fetch Klines fetches limit=50 1h candles per cycle: at 6h between runs, only ~6 new hourly candles land per cycle, well within the 50-candle window (~44-candle safety margin) -- the fetch always covers the full gap since the previous run. As a secondary backstop, runCycle is also a pure function of its input candles (no wall-clock reads), so if a cycle ever runs against unchanged/already-processed candles, repeated /api/cycle calls are idempotent no-ops (tests/cycle/idempotency.test.ts), not a correctness risk.

nodes.name: Acciones Symbols
nodes.notes: Acciones branch's single source of asset list (mirrors 'Symbols', the crypto branch's equivalent node). Emits one item per symbol; every downstream node in this branch runs once per item. /api/cycle validates each symbol via ACCIONES_SYMBOL_PATTERN (^[A-Z]{1,5}(\.[A-Z])?$, src/market/assets.ts), independent of any list, plus the shared MAX_ASSETS=25 cap applied per market. Adding or removing a ticker here needs no app-side change beyond staying within that cap. DO NOT RENAME this node: 'Set Acciones Symbol' recovers each item's symbol through $('Acciones Symbols').

nodes.name: Fetch Acciones Candles
nodes.notes: Raw fetch only (mirrors 'Fetch Klines', the crypto branch's equivalent node). ONE node for every US equity: n8n runs it once per input item, so the 'symbol' query value is the per-item expression {{ $json.symbol }} instead of a literal - adding a ticker needs no new node. outputsize=50 matches the system's uniform per-cycle window (see design.md 'Why 50'). MANUAL STEP - create a Query Auth credential named exactly 'Twelve Data API Key' with Name=apikey and Value=<your Twelve Data API key>, then select it here; apikey is supplied ONLY via this credential, never inline in this JSON (T-2 pattern, mirrors 'FAF Cycle Shared Secret'). onError routes a PER-ITEM Twelve Data failure/rate-limit to this node's dedicated ERROR output pin (main[1]), left intentionally unconnected, mirroring 'Fetch Klines'' isolation semantics. [MANUAL-VERIFICATION-ONLY, acciones-market-integration design.md]: Twelve Data's time_series response for a single symbol is a top-level JSON OBJECT ({meta, values, status}), not an array - per this exact workflow's own confirmed n8n behavior (see 'Fetch Klines' notes: n8n only auto-splits top-level ARRAY responses into one item per element; a top-level OBJECT response always yields exactly one item), this node should NOT need options.response.response.fullResponse=true the way 'Fetch Klines' needed it for Binance's raw array. This has NOT been confirmed against a live Twelve Data response yet - verify item count is exactly 1-per-symbol (not more) before activating this branch in production; if it explodes, apply the same fullResponse=true + read $json.body.values fallback 'Fetch Klines'/'Set Symbol' use.

nodes.name: Set Acciones Symbol
nodes.notes: Attaches this item's symbol plus the raw Twelve Data values array under a stable 'klines' field, so the Aggregate Acciones Payload Code node downstream never infers the asset from item order. Mirrors 'Set Symbol' (crypto branch). The symbol CANNOT be read from $json here: the HTTP Request node upstream replaced each item's json with Twelve Data's response body ({meta, values, status}). It is recovered by n8n item linking from the 'Acciones Symbols' node ($('Acciones Symbols').item), which resolves per item via pairedItem - so renaming 'Acciones Symbols' breaks this expression. klines reads $json.values directly (NOT $json.body.values) because Twelve Data's single-object response should not require fullResponse=true on 'Fetch Acciones Candles' upstream - this is a [MANUAL-VERIFICATION-ONLY] assumption, confirm it holds against a live response before activating this branch (see 'Fetch Acciones Candles' notes).

nodes.name: Aggregate Acciones Payload
nodes.notes: Only reshapes Twelve Data's string-valued values[] ({datetime,open,high,low,close,volume}) into the Candle[] shape app/api/cycle/route.ts expects ({symbol, klines:[{openTime,open,high,low,close,volume}]}), plus the top-level market:'acciones' discriminator (acciones-market-integration design.md D-A/D-C). No RDF, no indicator math, no decision logic here - all of that stays server-side, mirrors 'Aggregate (build /api/cycle payload)' (crypto branch). Reads item.json.symbol/item.json.klines directly, both attached by 'Set Acciones Symbol' upstream - no positional item-order inference.

nodes.name: POST /api/cycle (Acciones)
nodes.notes: Independent call from the crypto branch's 'POST /api/cycle' node - reuses the SAME shared-secret credential ('FAF Cycle Shared Secret'), same MANUAL STEP requirements (credential Name=x-faf-shared-secret and Value=<your FAF_CYCLE_SHARED_SECRET>). Payload carries market:'acciones' (from 'Aggregate Acciones Payload' upstream), so app/api/cycle/route.ts routes it to the acciones-keyed cache entry independently of the crypto branch's push (acciones-market-integration design.md D-A/D-B). T-2: the secret is NEVER stored in this JSON - n8n excludes credential values from workflow export.
